title: POC scoping: cost modeling & benchmarks with HelioSoft
next_steps: Redwood to send POC pricing worksheet and benchmark plan (Jordan)
HelioSoft to share sample workload + representative prompt set (Maya)
Schedule 1-week baseline benchmark run on Dedicated capacity (w/ Priya)
Follow-up meeting to review results and finalize success criteria - target 2026-04-25
action_items: Jordan Miles - send pricing spreadsheet and dedicated vs hosted delta - due 2026-04-20
Priya Kothari - prepare benchmark infra playbook + runbook and sample Jupyter notebook - due 2026-04-22
Maya Ruiz - provide 1000 representative queries, traffic distribution, and current latency histograms - due 2026-04-20
Tom Baxter - confirm networking constraints (VPC peering, egress) and security contacts - due 2026-04-21
summary: POC scoping focused on unit economics: per-token estimates for HelioSoft's mixed prompt/response workload, batching/caching knobs, and an agreed benchmark plan. Customer leans toward Dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation but needs clear per-token math to justify commit. Agreed to run a 1-week baseline on Redwood Dedicated and validate cost/latency tradeoffs.
topics: Batching, KV caching, and quantization knobs
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro — i'm jordan miles, AE for enterprise — with me is priya kothari, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Alex (HelioSoft, CTO): good, thanks. alex here. maya and tom are on as well.
[00:00:18] Maya (HelioSoft): hey all.
[00:00:20] Tom (HelioSoft): hello.
[00:00:25] Priya (Redwood SE): hi team. quick agenda — we want to align on your success criteria for the POC, get the workload sizing, and then walk through cost modeling and a benchmark plan. feel free to jump in.
[00:00:40] Alex: sounds good. high level — we're exploring a guided assistance feature inside our analytics UI. main asks are low latency for interactive sessions and keeping inference cost predictable. budget target is ~ $10k/month for inference to start, but we can iterate.
[00:00:58] Jordan: great. can you give us the current qps and average tokens per call today?
[00:01:07] Maya: so currently our batch offline scoring runs are separate. for the interactive feature we expect peak 80-120 qps, 95th percentile is important. prompt sizes — average prompt ~ 220 tokens, average generated response ~ 130 tokens. some long tails up to 2k tokens but rare.
[00:01:30] Priya: got it. that's a typical mixed workload. for cost modeling a few knobs matter: batching/latency SLOs, KV cache hit rates for repeated context, and model size/quantization. are you aiming for sub-200ms p95?
[00:01:44] Alex: ideally yes, <200ms p95. if that's not feasible we can tolerate up to 350ms but there'd be product tradeoffs.
[00:01:52] Jordan: for pricing we show both hosted per-token and Dedicated reserved capacity numbers. for your volume Dedicated tends to be more predictable and lowers per-token. we'll run numbers live soon.
[00:02:05] [00:02:05] Priya: quick note — our KV caching gives big wins for repeated prefixes; if your UI reuses prompt scaffolding across users we often see effective token reductions of 20-40% on average. sometimes transcription labels show K-V cash but it's KV cache.
[00:02:20] Maya: we do have a lot of reused scaffolding, so caching sounds promising. how do you reflect that in the per-token model?
[00:02:27] Priya: we model two numbers: raw tokens processed and billable tokens after cache hits. example: raw prompt 220 + response 130 = 350 tokens; with 30% cache hit on prompt prefix billable might be ~295 tokens. batching also reduces per-token compute cost but can increase tail latency.
[00:02:45] Alex: can you give a ballpark per-token numbers for hosted vs dedicated? rough numbers are fine now.
[00:02:52] Jordan: sure — ballpark: hosted API for a large LLM variant we commonly recommend is in the $0.0008-$0.0012 per token range end-to-end for mixed workloads; Dedicated can drop that to roughly $0.0004-$0.0007 per token depending on utilization, batching, and quantization. those are illustrative — we'll calculate for your exact mix.
[00:03:15] Tom: that delta is meaningful. but how much utilization do we need to hit the lower end?
[00:03:21] Priya: typically you need sustained utilization of 60-80% of reserved capacity during peak windows to amortize fixed costs. we factor in burst policies too. for POC we can model both a 50% and 75% utilization scenario to show sensitivity.
[00:03:36] Jordan: also note the Dedicated flow includes options for int8 quantized models which reduce GPU memory and can improve throughput, but sometimes at a small quality delta. we can propose quantization profiles for a subset of requests if you want.
[00:03:51] Maya: we care about quality — any reg tests you run?
[00:03:54] Priya: yes we run sample-based regressions tied to your prompt set. for POC we'll do side-by-side outputs and diff key metrics (bleu/rouge not perfect for chat, but we'll use embedding-similarity + manual review).
[00:04:10] [00:04:10] Alex: ok let's get into the benchmark plan. what environment do you want?
[00:04:14] Priya: for apples-to-apples: 1) run a baseline on Redwood Hosted for 24h to capture real infra variability, 2) run Dedicated baseline (reserved nodes) with the same prompts for 1 week to see sustained throughput and unit economics, 3) run a few quantization/ batching variants. we'll need a sample workload (Maya) and a small agents notebook from us.
[00:04:36] Jordan: timeline wise — if we get the dataset by 2026-04-20 we can spin up the baseline hosted run within 48 hours, and start Dedicated runs by 2026-04-22, finish initial POC by 2026-04-29. does that align with your internal timelines?
[00:04:48] Alex: yes that works; product team wants an answer before end of month.
[00:04:52] Tom: security question — Dedicated will be in a VPC, can you support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS? we have strict key management requirements.
[00:05:02] Jordan: yes — Dedicated supports VPC peering and integrates with customer KMS/HSM. we'll share our security pack. Priya, can you call out docs?
[00:05:10] Priya: sure — we'll share SOC2 and our Private deployment security brief. for a Dedicated POC we'll supply a security checklist for the infra team.
[00:05:20] Maya: great. back to costs — walk me through an example per-request math with batching.
[00:05:25] Priya: example: assume billable tokens per request after cache 295 as earlier. on Dedicated, if we achieve median batch size of 4 during peaks, per-token compute amortized drops by roughly 20-30% compared to single-request mode. so effective per-request compute cost might be equivalent to 295 tokens * $0.0005 = $0.1475. with hosted that's 295 * $0.0009 = $0.2655. multiply by expected QPS and hours to get monthly.
[00:05:48] Alex: that checks. can we model tail cases where latency SLO pushes batching down and we lose batching efficiency?
[00:05:55] Priya: yes we model two latency profiles: conservative (tight SLO, minimal batching) and relaxed (allow batching up to 100ms additional queueing). we'll show 95th pct latency and cost tradeoffs.
[00:06:06] [00:06:06] Jordan: also mention KV cache hit sensitivity — we should show scenarios at 10%, 30%, and 50% prompt cache hit to show savings.
[00:06:14] Maya: how do you account for tokenization differences and different model flavors? we might evaluate smaller model variants for cheaper inference.
[00:06:22] Priya: we include model family tiers in the workbook. tokenization differences show up as average tokens per request. we'll run the sample prompts against each candidate model to get actual token counts. smaller models reduce cost but increase latency for some tasks; quality regression tests guide that choice.
[00:06:36] Tom: what about cold-starts or KV-cache warmup? first hour might be worse.
[00:06:40] Priya: we'll capture warmup in the 1-week Dedicated run; we'll also instrument KPIs like cache hit over time. for cost modeling we include a warmup multiplier for week 1.
[00:06:51] Alex: network egress cost? if Dedicated is in our VPC, we still have egress charges for large responses. how do you show that?
[00:06:58] Jordan: egress is customer-specific; we'll include a placeholder for estimated egress per-token (typically small) and leave a line item for cloud egress. Tom, please confirm your network billing so we can plug numbers in.
[00:07:08] Tom: will do.
[00:07:12] [00:07:12] Maya: ok, on acceptance criteria: product wants p95 latency <250ms, cost per active user <$1/month at expected usage, and output quality no worse than X (we'll give a qualitative bar). can we map to those?
[00:07:25] Priya: yes we'll map the benchmark outputs to those success metrics. for cost per active user we need monthly MAU and per-user messages. send that in the worksheet.
[00:07:35] Alex: we're leaning Dedicated because of latency guarantees and data isolation. show both options so leadership can see ROI.
[00:07:42] Jordan: absolutely. we'll produce a summarized one-pager: decision matrix Hosted vs Dedicated vs Hybrid with numbers.
[00:07:49] [00:07:49] Priya: technical note — if you want hard 150ms p95 we may need to reserve more capacity or use smaller model variants; there's a cost tradeoff.
[00:07:58] Maya: for user experience, 200-250ms is acceptable at first.
[00:08:03] Jordan: cool. any blockers on data sharing for the prompt set?
[00:08:07] Maya: no blockers. we'll scrub PII but give representative prompts.
[00:08:11] Tom: on compliance, we'll need to loop in our security team; please include contact point in the pack.
[00:08:16] Priya: will do.
[00:08:20] [00:08:20] Jordan: quick aside — competitors were mentioned in your RFP?
[00:08:24] Alex: some teams looked at OpenAI and Anthropic. Cognizant evaluated Cohere as well. main difference for us is cost predictability and private tenancy.
[00:08:35] Priya: noted. we'll emphasize rollouts, audit logs, and KMS in the docs.
[00:08:40] [00:08:40] Jordan: ok let's walk through a sample line-item calc. i'll read numbers and priya will clarify assumptions.
[00:08:46] Jordan: baseline: 100 qps steady for 4 hours/day peak, average billable tokens per request 295, monthly peak hours 120. Hosted per-token $0.0009, Dedicated effective $0.0005. compute monthly token count = 100 qps * 3600 * 4 * 30 * 295 = big number — we won't calc here verbally, we'll put in the sheet.
[00:09:06] Priya: right i'll run the workbook. example quick calc: 100 qps * 4 hours/day * 30 days = 432,000 requests. multiply by 295 tokens = ~127M tokens. at $0.0009 that's $114k/month hosted; at $0.0005 that's $63.5k/month on Dedicated before amortization and reserved discounts. numbers show why commit decisions matter.
[00:09:30] Maya: that's higher than our initial $10k target. what's the knob to reduce to 10k?
[00:09:35] Priya: options: reduce model size, aggressive caching (increase cache hit to 50%), increase batching (accept slightly higher latency), or reduce peak concurrency with frontend queueing. each has UX/quality tradeoffs.
[00:09:46] Alex: can we do a hybrid approach, host low-sensitivity requests on Hosted cheaper model and sensitive low-latency on Dedicated?
[00:09:53] Jordan: yes, smart routing can split by route/latency. we can show a hybrid cost projection.
[00:09:58] [00:09:58] Tom: for the Dedicated POC, how much lead time to provision nodes?
[00:10:02] Priya: typically 48-72 hours once we agree on the spec and networking.
[00:10:06] Alex: ok. next steps recap?
[00:10:09] Jordan: Jordan sends pricing workbook and one-pager decision matrix (action). Priya sends benchmark runbook and notebook. Maya to share prompt set and traffic histograms. Tom to share networking/security contacts. schedule follow-up week of 2026-04-25.
[00:10:22] Maya: sounds good.
[00:10:24] Alex: thanks all.
[00:10:28] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up by email with links: pricing workbook, benchmark notebook, security pack (links: https://redwood.ai/poc/pricing-workbook, https://redwood.ai/poc/benchmark-notebook, https://redwood.ai/security).
[00:10:42] Priya: quick footnote — we'll include sensitivity charts for cache hit, batching median, and utilization.
[00:10:49] Alex: perfect. thanks.
[00:10:53] [00:10:53] -- end of recorded portion (we kept it to the first 11 minutes of the call for notes) --
[00:11:00] [note]: longer technical deep-dive followed after call where Priya and Tom iterated on networking details and an initial per-node sizing. that portion is summarized in the runbook.
